item.title: Humanoid robot beats men's 100m world record in Beijing
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-23
BEIJING, Aug. 22 (Xinhua) -- A humanoid robot clocked 9.39 seconds to beat the men's 100m world record of 9.58 seconds during the opening ceremony of the second edition of the World Humanoid Robot Games at the National Speed Skating Oval in Beijing on Saturday.
The men's 100m world record is 9.58 seconds, set by Usain Bolt in Berlin in 2009.
The record-breaking performance marked the start of competition among humanoid robots. Featuring 51 events with a total of 1,301 competitions, the Games attracted 666 teams with 2,056 humanoid robots from around the world, with the number of teams up 138 percent from the inaugural edition last year.
In addition to athletics and football events, the Games also introduced new events including weightlifting, tug-of-war and table tennis, putting the robots' physical structures and core components to the test.
Running from Saturday to Wednesday, the Games also expanded scenario-based competitions designed to simulate real-world applications, covering sectors such as logistics, hospitality and household services to help robots better integrate into people's daily lives.
In April, a humanoid robot from Shenzhen Honor Smart Technology Development Co., Ltd. won the Beijing E-Town half-marathon in 50 minutes and 26 seconds in autonomous navigation mode, beating the human world record of 57:20.
As humanoid robot research and development continues to make breakthroughs, the "Ice Ribbon," where a world record was set during the Beijing 2022 Winter Olympics, is now hosting another showcase of advances in humanoid robotics.

item.title: Chinese robotics fair draws crowds as industry brews innovation
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-23
A robot and a staff member demonstrate human-robot collaboration during the 2026 World Robot Conference in Beijing, capital of China, Aug. 20, 2026. (Xinhua/Xie Han)
BEIJING, Aug. 22 (Xinhua) -- Unitree Robotics' blockbuster IPO, the bustling World Robot Conference (WRC), and the upcoming World Humanoid Robot Games, amount to a string of high-profile events which have combined to make this week a "super week" for Chinese robotics.
Underpinning these events is a clear trend: China is swiftly becoming a global epicenter of robotics innovation, which is poised to reshape the way products are manufactured and the way people live.
The numbers confirm China's significant rise in robotics. Data from the country's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology show that revenue of industrial enterprises above designated size in China's robotics sector had exceeded 300 billion yuan (about 44.24 billion U.S. dollars) in 2025, with an average annual growth rate of more than 20 percent over the past five years.
Also, a report by California-based research firm Smart Analytics Global indicates that global humanoid robot shipments totaled approximately 19,100 units in the first half of 2026, with Chinese-made units accounting for over 97 percent of the total.
A robotic smartphone assembly and quality inspection line is displayed at the 2026 World Robot Conference (WRC) in Beijing, capital of China, Aug. 20, 2026. (Xinhua/Ju Huanzong)
More broadly, exports of industrial robots increased 13.2 percent in the January-July period, while shipments of surgical robots surged 3.3-fold year on year in the first half of 2026.
Robots, AI products and innovative drugs are three new drivers of China's export growth, according to Science and Technology Minister Yin Hejun. This momentum has played out at this year's WRC, which is being held in a southeastern technology hub in Beijing.
On weekday mornings, traffic ground to a halt for kilometers around the WRC exhibition hall, forcing the organizers to issue daily "travel advisories," a task that speaks volumes about the sector's red-hot vitality in China. Inside the venue, crowds are so dense they rival the throngs at CES in Las Vegas.
A robot gives a drink to a staff member during the 2026 World Robot Conference in Beijing, capital of China, Aug. 20, 2026. (Xinhua/Xie Han)
WRC exhibitors this year have topped 300, up 69 percent from 2025, with the event featuring over 3,000 products, and roughly 300 making their debuts. Additionally, many are powered by large AI models, cloud computing and big data.
China's vast and sophisticated manufacturing sector is providing a massive testing ground for embodied AI technologies, which are now being deployed on a large scale in factories and training facilities.
According to an industry research report, by June this year, China had launched over 70 training grounds for robots, with another 46 either under construction or in the planning pipeline.
"This week's IPO is just the start of the journey," said Aron Kisdi, managing director of Autodiscovery and Unitree Robotics' U.K. distributor, at the company's WRC booth. Unitree Robotics, based in Hangzhou in east China, went public on China's A-share market on Wednesday, the same day the WRC opened, and its shares skyrocketed 629.44 percent to open at 1,100 yuan.
"It signals that the time in the lab is nearing an end, and we're pushing robots into the real world," Kisdi explained.
People visit the 2026 World Robot Conference in Beijing, capital of China, Aug. 19, 2026. (Xinhua/Zhang Chenlin)
On the exhibition floor at the WRC, many booths are displaying robots operating in real-world work scenarios. A logistics robot sorts parcels at a rate of more than 1,000 items per hour, while nearby, a pair of dexterous robotic hands smoothly folds a cardboard sheet into a packaging box.
At UBTECH's display zone, robots perform automated loading and unloading of automotive sheet metal parts with zero human oversight, building on earlier trials at several car plants. Chinese robotics firms have, notably, already put robots into factories to test their capability of doing more sophisticated jobs beyond just basic handling.
Elsewhere at the show, automakers like Xiaomi feature their own humanoid robots, underscoring how industry demand is fueling robotics innovation.
The bustling expo floor in Beijing also features robots designed for emotional companionship, housework, convenience-store retail and coffee brewing, which can tap into China's massive consumer market, the world's second-largest in terms of commodity consumption for more than 10 consecutive years.
"Robots are no longer only about flashy concepts and specs. They're increasingly focused on tackling real-life challenges," said Ren Jingwei, a manager at Zhiyuan Research Institute in Hangzhou.
A child interacts with a companion robot during the 2026 World Robot Conference in Beijing, capital of China, Aug. 20, 2026. (Xinhua/Ju Huanzong)
Also, this year's WRC fair is no longer just for curious onlookers. Industry players up and down the supply chain are busy exchanging business cards and phone numbers there in bids to forge new partnerships.
One noteworthy shift this year is the considerable presence of dexterous-hand sensor makers, joint module suppliers and chip manufacturers at the WRC. These component suppliers, once supporters behind finished robots, have now also taken center stage in their own niche sectors -- a sign that China's robotics industry is maturing into a more sophisticated ecosystem.
Humanoid robots could spur investment across precision transmission, smart sensors, AI chips and intelligent software, generating a huge market from R&D to after-sales service, said Xu Xiaolan from the Chinese Institute of Electronics.
To many attendees, Beijing's robot show points to an upcoming transformative change in the industry. The "ChatGPT moment" for embodied AI will come in two to three years under an optimistic outlook, or within five to ten years at the latest, said Wang Xingxing, Unitree Robotics founder and CEO, when speaking at a WRC forum.

item.title: China's top anti-graft body vows higher standards, more concrete measures to advance its work
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-23
Li Xi, a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and secretary of the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection (CCDI), addresses the sixth plenary session of the 20th CCDI of the CPC in Beijing, capital of China, Aug. 22, 2026. (Xinhua/Yue Yuewei)
BEIJING, Aug. 22 (Xinhua) -- The sixth plenary session of the 20th Central Commission for Discipline Inspection (CCDI) of the Communist Party of China (CPC) was held in Beijing on Saturday.
Li Xi, a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and secretary of the CCDI, addressed the session.
The session called for steadfastly following the Chinese path to combat corruption and advance the high-quality development of discipline inspection and supervision work in the new era, with higher standards and more concrete measures.
The session reviewed discipline inspection and supervision work in the first half of 2026 and made further arrangements to ensure the effective implementation of relevant tasks.
It called for strengthening political oversight, deepening political inspections, strictly enforcing discipline in leadership transitions, unswervingly improving conduct, enforcing discipline and combating corruption, and continuing concentrated rectification of misconduct and corruption at the people's doorsteps, to ensure the high-quality completion of all tasks for the year.
The session elected Zhao Shiyong deputy secretary of the CCDI, and Zhang Zhong deputy secretary of the CCDI and a member of its Standing Committee.

item.title: Macao SAR releases economic, social development plan for 2026-2030 period
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-22
This photo taken on Aug. 18, 2026 shows a press conference held to introduce the Third Five-Year Plan for Economic and Social Development of the Macao Special Administrative Region (SAR) in south China's Macao. The Macao SAR government on Tuesday released the Third Five-Year Plan for Economic and Social Development of the Macao SAR (2026-2030). (Xinhua/Cheong Kam Ka)
MACAO, Aug. 18 (Xinhua) -- The Macao Special Administrative Region (SAR) government on Tuesday released the Third Five-Year Plan for Economic and Social Development of the Macao SAR (2026-2030).
The third five-year plan is an important initiative for Macao to advance the cause of "one country, two systems" and better integrate into and serve the country's overall development, said Macao SAR Chief Executive Sam Hou Fai at a press conference held at the SAR government headquarters to introduce the plan.
The plan, consisting of 10 parts and 36 chapters, sets out eight development goals, which are: to ensure full implementation of the holistic approach to national security; to improve the effectiveness of law-based governance; to make substantial progress in appropriate economic diversification; to advance progress with high-quality development of the Guangdong-Macao In-Depth Cooperation Zone in Hengqin; to yield visible results from the integrated development of education, technology and talent; to further improve people's well-being; to make significant progress in building a beautiful and "smart" Macao; and to better integrate into and serve the country's overall development.
The chief executive said that the SAR government is proactively positioning and planning Macao within the broader context of national development and actively implementing the country's 15th Five-Year Plan's relevant arrangements.
Sam outlined four major tasks for the 2026-2030 period: to advance appropriate economic diversification through major projects and a government guidance fund; to deepen integrated development with Hengqin and advance high-quality development of the cooperation zone; to accelerate urban renewal and build a beautiful and "smart" Macao; and to reinforce Macao's connectivity with both the mainland and the world, and better integrate into and serve the country's overall development.
The release followed a public consultation conducted from May 20 to June 28, during which the SAR government solicited opinions and suggestions from various sectors of society.
Yin Yifen, director of Social, Economic and Public Policy Research Center, Macao Polytechnic University, told Xinhua that Macao's five-year planning mechanism "brings two core advantages for economic diversification and policy coherence."
Yin added that the mechanism operates within the "one country, two systems" and serves as an important institutional supplement to the framework. It anchors Macao's development in national strategies while translating broad requirements into measurable goals covering the economy, people's livelihoods and security, and consolidating institutional capacity for SAR governance.

item.title: Macao's new five-year plan charts course for high-quality development
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-22
This photo taken on Aug. 18, 2026 shows a press conference held to introduce the Third Five-Year Plan for Economic and Social Development of the Macao Special Administrative Region (SAR) in south China's Macao. (Xinhua/Cheong Kam Ka)
MACAO, Aug. 19 (Xinhua) -- Macao's new development plan for the 2026-2030 period marks another key step in the successful practice of "one country, two systems" with Macao characteristics and is significant for advancing its appropriate economic diversification.
The Macao Special Administrative Region (SAR) government on Tuesday released the Third Five-Year Plan for Economic and Social Development of the Macao SAR (2026-2030) -- a roadmap for the SAR to march toward high-quality development and a major move to actively align with the national 15th Five-Year Plan.
The five-year period represents a critical window for Macao's high-quality development. The new blueprint will translate national strategic opportunities into driving forces for Macao's development, and turn institutional strengths into governance efficacy.
At its core is the push for appropriate economic diversification -- a move to address Macao's structural challenge due to its long-standing reliance on the gaming industry. The SAR will foster emerging industries as new growth drivers through major projects and a government guidance fund, and advance high-quality development in the Guangdong-Macao In-Depth Cooperation Zone in Hengqin.
Notably, the blueprint balances economic development with social priorities. Education, employment, housing, elderly care and urban renewal receive dedicated policy attention, embodying a people-centered approach that ensures the fruits of development are shared more widely and equitably among all citizens.
From the proactive planning of the SAR government to the suggestions from all sectors of society, the new guiding document fully attests to the fine tradition of "loving the motherland and loving Macao" -- the very source of Macao's resolve to surmount difficulties and forge ahead.
Macao strictly fulfills its constitutional duties and aligns with national strategies, while exploring its development path based on its unique endowments. The new development roadmap clearly shows that under the principle of "patriots administering Macao," Macao is adept at integrating central government support, institutional strengths, and social synergy to continuously translate institutional advantages into tangible governance outcomes.
As the Macao SAR government translates the roadmap into reality through concerted efforts across all sectors of society, the city will surely open up new prospects for high-quality development, contribute more to national rejuvenation, and ensure the steady and sustained practice of "one country, two systems" with Macao characteristics.

item.title: Xi congratulates Hichilema on re-election as Zambian president
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-21
BEIJING, Aug. 20 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday congratulated Hakainde Hichilema on his re-election as president of Zambia.
In his message, Xi said that they have met twice in recent years, and jointly steered the development of China-Zambia relations.
The political mutual trust between the two countries has continued to deepen, practical cooperation has been fruitful, and China and Zambia have closely coordinated and cooperated in multilateral affairs, he said.
Xi said he attaches great importance to the development of China-Zambia ties, and stands ready to work with Hichilema to implement the outcomes of the Beijing Summit of the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation.
He also pledged to join the Zambian leader in carrying forward traditional friendship, cementing mutual support, and continuously raising the level of mutually beneficial cooperation, so as to take the China-Zambia comprehensive strategic cooperative partnership to new heights and deliver greater benefits to the two peoples.

item.title: China's top legislator holds talks with president of El Salvador's Legislative Assembly
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-21
Zhao Leji, chairman of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (NPC), holds talks with Ernesto Castro, president of El Salvador's Legislative Assembly, at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Aug. 20, 2026. (Xinhua/Rao Aimin)
BEIJING, Aug. 20 (Xinhua) -- Zhao Leji, chairman of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (NPC), held talks with Ernesto Castro, president of El Salvador's Legislative Assembly, in Beijing on Thursday.
Noting that August 21 this year marks the 8th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between China and El Salvador, Zhao said that China stands ready to work with the Salvadoran side to implement the important common understandings reached by the heads of state of the two countries and elevate bilateral relations to new heights.
Both sides should deepen political mutual trust and be friends who support each other, he said, adding China appreciates El Salvador's adherence to the one-China principle and its support for China's position regarding Taiwan and human rights.
Zhao called on both sides to focus on the well-being of the people, deepen exchanges and cooperation in education, culture, media and other fields, and strengthen multilateral coordination and safeguard common interests.
The NPC of China is ready to work with the Legislative Assembly of El Salvador to enhance friendly exchanges between their special committees, bilateral friendship groups, deputies to the NPC and legislators, share experience in areas such as the rule of law and poverty reduction and development, and provide legal safeguards for practical cooperation, said Zhao.
For his part, Castro stated that developing friendly relations with China is of great significance to El Salvador. The Legislative Assembly of El Salvador is ready to strengthen mutual learning through exchanges with the NPC of China, building a bridge for further developing bilateral relations and advancing practical cooperation, said Castro.

item.title: Xi congratulates Baka on assuming Hungarian presidency
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-20
BEIJING, Aug. 19 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Wednesday extended congratulations to Andras Baka on his assuming the office as Hungary's president.
In his message, Xi said Hungary, one of the first countries to recognize the People's Republic of China, shares a long-standing traditional friendship with China.
Since the establishment of diplomatic relations 77 years ago, both countries have always adhered to mutual respect, equality, mutual benefit and win-win cooperation, and achieved remarkable results in collaboration across various fields, he said.
Xi said he attaches great importance to developing China-Hungary ties and stands ready to work with Baka to carry forward the traditional friendship, deepen mutual political trust and practical cooperation in all areas, and promote the steady and long-term development of the all-weather comprehensive strategic partnership for the new era between China and Hungary, so as to better benefit the two peoples.

item.title: China's wild Asian elephant population nears 400
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-14
Thanks to sustained conservation efforts, China's wild Asian elephant population has more than doubled over the past four decades to nearly 400, according to the latest data from the National Forestry and Grassland Administration (NFGA).
